text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- SAO PAULO HAS TO INVEST, SAYS NAKANO

After two years cleaning up its finances, Brazil's wealthiest state gets ready to resume investments in 1997. "The government has entered a new phase in which it has to invest, it can no longer avoid it," says Yoshiaki Nakano, Sao Paulo's Finance Secretary.
The state public sector is likely to invest 6.8 billion reais in 1997, especially in health, education, housing and transportation.
-- TELEBRAS IS BLUE-CHIP IN THE U.S.

Telebras shares were the second most traded among foreign firms listed on U.S. stock exchanges. Deals with Telebras amounted to $26.8 billion in the company's first year of trade on the NYSE. The most traded foreign firm was Royal Dutch Petroleum.
-- BLOCKBUSTER ISSUES $30 MLN IN BONDS
Blockbuster Video do Brasil has issued $30 million in Eurobonds to meet its target of reaching 170 stores by the end of the year 2000.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- HEALTH EXPENSES PER INHABITANT DROP

The government's health expenses per capita fell to $88.70 last year from $95.97 in 1995. During its electoral campaign, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso promised to spend 80 reais per inhabitant in health projects.
-- BANK SEES $11 BLN IN FOREIGN CAPITAL INFLOWS THIS YEAR
Brazil is expected to receive $11 billion in foreign capital this year, according to Henrique Meirelles, BankBoston president. Last year, the country received $9 billion.
-- RAINS LEAVE 31,000 HOMELESS
Rains in Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro states have left more than 31,000 people homeless in the last five days. Sixty-six people died in Minas Gerais and over 26,000 are homeless.
O GLOBO
-- RIO MAYOR OFFICE WILL TRY TO REMOVE 700 FAMILIES FROM RISKY AREAS
Rio de Janeiro city mayor office will notify today the first 300 families of 700, asking them to leave their homes immediately because of the risk of landslides caused by heavy rains.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
